name: How much clearance do I need around a kitchen island?

mainEntity.name: How much clearance do I need around a kitchen island after a layout change?
mainEntity.text: How much clearance do I need around a kitchen island after a layout change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Island clearance should be planned around real movement, not just the island’s size on paper. There needs to be enough room for cabinet doors, dishwasher doors, oven doors, and refrigerator doors to open without collision. There also needs to be a comfortable walking path for the people using the kitchen at the same time. In a busy kitchen, tight clearances create daily frustration, especially when two people are cooking or when guests pass through the space. The island should support prep, seating, or storage without interrupting the triangle or creating a bottleneck. If the room cannot support the needed clearance, a smaller island, a peninsula, or a different cabinet arrangement may work better. Good design prioritizes circulation first, then sizes the island to fit the remaining space. That approach usually produces a kitchen that feels larger and functions better than one that is overfilled.
acceptedAnswer.description: A kitchen island needs enough surrounding space for doors to open, people to pass, and drawers to use comfortably. If clearance is too tight, the island becomes an obstacle instead of a useful work zone, especially in kitchens with multiple users or appliance doors that swing outward.
